channel.title: MediaToday Co Ltd - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from MediaToday Co Ltd (maltatoday.com.mt)

item.title: Deborah Schembri to contest general election with Labour Party in political comeback
item.description: Former parliamentary secretary Deborah Schembri says she has accepted prime minister’s invitation to contest general election with Labour Party • Schembri did not contest last election

item.title: Man pleads guilty after motorised bicycle collision leaves teenager permanently injured
item.description: 22-year-old man from Lija released on bail after traffic collision that left a 16-year-old boy with permanent injuries, including the loss of a testicle

item.title: Wife forgives husband, wants reconciliation despite ‘severe’ risk assessment
item.description: Victim tells court she will take responsibility to avoid future incidents caused by external stress, declines protection order

item.title: Tighter rules on cannabis stock introduced
item.description: Clubs with over 350 members will be able to hold 3.5kg of cannabis under new rules

item.title: Man admits to dangerous driving without licence or insurance
item.description: 23-year-old man admitted to driving without a licence or insurance in Żejtun and will be sentenced later this month

item.title: Man caught with two grams of cannabis and two grams of cocaine charged with trafficking
item.description: Court denies bail to man accused of possessing cocaine and cannabis in circumstances indicating trafficking, as investigations into third parties continue

item.title: Second alleged victim recounts threats, passports withheld in trafficking case against Fabio Vespa
item.description: A Colombian woman tells court she was promised cleaning work but ended up in prostitution, as passports were allegedly withheld and thousands of euros demanded in the trafficking case against Fabio Vespa

item.title: Policy opens ODZ quarries to sports complexes and supermarkets
item.description: A draft policy proposes allowing development of sports facilities in ODZ quarries with 40% of floor space dedicated to commercial activities including supermarkets

item.title: Notary victims: Ombudsman points to three years of inaction, minister ‘optimistic’ solution will be found
item.description: Justice Minister Jonathan Attard is 'optimistic' the government will find a “reasonable and just solution” for victims of notaries who fail to register property sales, but Ombudsman Joseph Zammit McKeon says his office had made recommendations in 2023 after concluding an investigation into the matter but these were never implemented by the authorities

item.title: We’re living in a crazy world
item.description: So, please, Mr Prime Minister stop targeting teenagers for votes with these hare-brained schemes… we are coping with enough crazy as it is
